Outcome_metric: Elemental carbon (PM2.5) attributed to the PMF traffic factor, 2009/2010 vs 2006/2007
Peer_reviewed_citation: Qadir, R. M., Abbaszade, G., Schnelle-Kreis, J., Chow, J. C., & Zimmermann, R. (2013). Concentrations and source contributions of particulate organic matter before and after implementation of a low emission zone in Munich, Germany. Environmental Pollution, 175, 158-167.
Stringency_note: Stage 1 (vehicles without any emission sticker excluded); city also had a heavy goods transit ban from Feb 2008
Extractor_notes: PM2.5 filter samples collected within the Munich LEZ (single site, type not stated in sources read) in 2006/2007 (before) and 2009/2010 (after); no control site. Average traffic-factor EC fell from 1.1 to 0.5 ug/m3; pct computed by extractor (-0.6/1.1). Abstract also reports total EC and several wood-burning markers significantly lower after; levoglucosan, retene and O-PAH higher. Years = approx midpoint of 2009/2010 sampling since Oct 2008. Abstract read via US EPA HERO record and the LMU/Helmholtz dissertation summary; publisher page not accessible. Weather not stated as controlled.

Outcome_metric: Half-hourly PM10, index stations inside zone vs reference station(s) outside, Oct 2008 to Jan 2009 vs Oct 2007 to Jan 2008, multiplicative model
Peer_reviewed_citation: Morfeld, P., Stern, R., Builtjes, P., Groneberg, D. A., & Spallek, M. (2013). Einrichtung einer Umweltzone und ihre Wirksamkeit auf die PM10-Feinstaubkonzentration: Eine Pilotanalyse am Beispiel München [Introduction of a low-emission zone and the effect on air pollutant concentration of particulate matter (PM10): A pilot study in Munich]. Zentralblatt für Arbeitsmedizin, Arbeitsschutz und Ergonomie, 63(2), 104-115.
Stringency_note: Stage 1 (vehicles without any emission sticker excluded); city also had a heavy goods transit ban from Feb 2008
Extractor_notes: Matched quadruples (26,438) difference-score design with regression adjustment for inversion base height, precipitation and wind speed; 5 index stations inside zone vs reference station outside (English abstract says 2, German abstract says 1). Raw means rose 33.9 to 39.0 ug/m3 inside and 24.6 to 30.5 outside. Additive model +0.017 ug/m3 (95% CI -0.33 to +0.37). Multiplicative -0.5% with CI printed as (-0.12%, +0.30%), which does not contain the point estimate (likely typo in abstract). not significant. Authors note results differ from Cyrys et al. 2009 using the same data. Distinct from Morfeld et al. 2014 19-city pooled study already in database.

Outcome_metric: City-level NO2 (UBA), average post-ban gap actual minus synthetic, to Jul 2022
Peer_reviewed_citation: Mirzoyan, N., Ott, I., & Castro, J. R. (2025). Diesel bans and urban air quality: A causal study of NO2 emissions in Germany using synthetic control. Sustainable Futures, 10, 101143.
Stringency_note: Diesel ban within Umweltzone, start 1 Jan 2019 as dated in paper
Extractor_notes: Synthetic control on monthly city-level NO2 from UBA (daily data aggregated), Jan 2012 to Jul 2022; donor pool of 13 German cities without bans; covariates employment, GDP per capita, diesel car share, commuter share. Outcome described as NO2 'per capita' but effects reported in ug/m3; scaling unclear and no city baseline reported, so pct could not be computed. Whether monitors lie on banned streets not stated. Absolute effect -30.06 ug/m3 (baseline SCM); ASCM -22.82, GSCM -19.24, SDiD -11.79. Donors Braunschweig 0.267, Ludwigshafen 0.235, Nuremberg 0.498. Placebo rank p = 1/14 (0.07), authors note this misses 5%; SDiD placebo bounds called significant. Effect_pct left blank because baseline not reported (not because non-significant).
